verdict.heading: Black Giant page, October measurements: EnergyX → this demo
verdict.summary: {fact:lh-bg-video-total} of {fact:lh-bg-weight} is two video files. The rest of the page — design, images, code — is {fact:lh-bg-other-bytes}.

intro: The whole argument on one page: what EnergyX's pages transfer and why, what this demo changes, what it cannot prove, and what the fact registry turned up. Every figure links to its source.

whyPlain.heading: Why this looks plain
whyPlain.body: A good-looking animated site is the easy half. The result usually looks like a lot of modern sites do: beautiful, and slow. Measured today, same tool, same region, same hour: energyx.com's Black Giant page scores {fact:lh2-ex-bg-perf} and takes {fact:lh2-ex-bg-lcp} to render its main content on a phone. This demo's version scores {fact:lh2-demo-bg-perf} and takes {fact:lh2-demo-bg-lcp}. That gap isn't about design, it's about delivery: large video files served as single full-size downloads instead of encoded and served poster-first. The footage isn't the problem; the pipeline around it is, and that's an engineering problem, not a creative one. So this build spent its budget on the parts that are hard to fake: every number traced to the EnergyX page it came from, a refusal that runs before the model does, and a check that caught one of my own drafts calling a grant 'backing'. The whole animation budget was {fact:demo-css-caught-claim} of compressed CSS, and it went to showing that check working. The cinematic version is a day of work on top of this, and it stays fast, because the speed budget is enforced in the build.
whyPlain.notesHeading: Measured 2026-11-10, and what it does not cover
notes: One run per page on lighthouse-metrics.com, Lighthouse 13.5.0, mobile preset, US West. Lab measurements, not field data. Each figure's source is the saved report, because the check page is account-scoped and not publicly shareable. The October measurements are kept as they were, each with its own date.

This demo's home page: score {fact:lh2-demo-home-perf}, main content in {fact:lh2-demo-home-lcp}, layout shift {fact:lh2-demo-home-cls}. Its Total Blocking Time was {fact:lh2-demo-home-tbt}, against the project's budget of {fact:budget-tbt}. That is over the budget. It was a single run, and across the six test regions in that run Total Blocking Time ranged from {fact:lh2-demo-home-tbt-range}. The budget is unchanged.
This demo's Black Giant page: score {fact:lh2-demo-bg-perf}, main content in {fact:lh2-demo-bg-lcp}, blocking time {fact:lh2-demo-bg-tbt}, layout shift {fact:lh2-demo-bg-cls}.
energyx.com's home page: score {fact:lh2-ex-home-perf}, main content in {fact:lh2-ex-home-lcp}, blocking time {fact:lh2-ex-home-tbt}, layout shift {fact:lh2-ex-home-cls}.

energyx.com's Black Giant page: score {fact:lh2-ex-bg-perf}, main content in {fact:lh2-ex-bg-lcp}, blocking time {fact:lh2-ex-bg-tbt}, layout shift {fact:lh2-ex-bg-cls}. The score is essentially unchanged since October ({fact:lh-bg-perf} then, {fact:lh2-ex-bg-perf} now), so the October analysis on this page still holds.
Page weight was not re-measured on 2026-11-10. Every byte figure on this page is from the October measurements.
I didn't optimise this demo for SEO. It is noindexed on purpose, so a low SEO score is expected and isn't part of what's being compared.

payload.heading: Where the bytes go
body: EnergyX's Black Giant page transfers {fact:lh-bg-weight} on a first visit. Of that, {fact:lh-bg-video-total} is two video files. Everything else on the page together comes to {fact:lh-bg-other-bytes}. These byte figures are from the 2026-10-08 measurement; page weight was not re-measured on 2026-11-10.

So the page is not heavy because it is rich. The design, copy and images are a small slice of the total. The weight is two finished videos reaching the browser as large single downloads, because there is no delivery step between the footage and the page. The homepage has the same shape.

comparison.intro: The Black Giant page as EnergyX serves it, and as this demo delivers it: a still poster first, video only after the page has loaded.
comparison.caption: Lighthouse lab results, Black Giant page (EnergyX measured 2026-10-08, this demo 2026-10-19)

A later, single-run re-measurement of 2026-11-10 is in the section above; page weight was not re-measured then, so the bytes here are from October.

bundle.heading: How much JavaScript this demo ships
bundle.verdict: Every page of this demo loads about the same amount of JavaScript: {fact:demo-js-home} on the home page and {fact:demo-js-black-giant} on the Black Giant page, the heaviest. Both are inside the project's first-load budget. The Black Giant page has {fact:demo-js-bg-headroom} to spare.
bundle.method: These are local measurements: a production build served on a laptop with next start. They are not measurements of the deployed site. The October Lighthouse figures for energyx.com and for this site, used elsewhere on this page, are separate measurements of deployed pages, made with a different tool.
bundle.detailSummary: How it was measured, what is in it, and what we left alone
bundle.basisHeading: How the figures in the list were measured
bundle.factsLink: Source and approval state for each figure are on the facts page.
detail: About {fact:demo-js-framework-share} of it is React DOM and the Next.js app-router client: the framework every page needs before any of this site's own code runs. The one script that is purely this site's own code is about {fact:demo-js-own-chunk-share}. That is a floor, not a total: the mobile menu and the hero video share files with framework code and were not separated out. Files were attributed by the library they contain, not module by module.
The Black Giant page loads one script the other pages do not, {fact:demo-js-bg-only-chunk}. It holds next/image and the hero video player. How the two split was not measured.

We considered replacing next/image with a plain image tag to remove it, and declined. The Black Giant page is inside the budget, and its image is the largest-contentful-paint element, the part that decides how fast the page feels. Changing how it loads would put that measured load time at risk to recover bytes the budget does not ask for. The margin is thin, so this is revisited if the page grows.

caveats.heading: What these numbers do not show
points: The video on this demo's Black Giant page is a placeholder: a short public-domain NASA clip, not EnergyX's footage. EnergyX's hero file alone is {fact:lh-bg-hero-video}. The placeholder is far smaller, so this demo's total says nothing about how small EnergyX's own video would be once prepared for the web.

Deferring the video fixes the Largest Contentful Paint: the first screen no longer waits for a video. It does not reduce the bytes. A phone that goes on to play the video still downloads all of it. Cutting the payload takes re-encoding, at sizes and in formats made for phones. That is the second half of the fix, and it has not been done here on EnergyX's files.

All of this is lab data: Lighthouse on one emulated phone over a throttled connection. It is repeatable, which makes it useful for before and after, but it is not what real visitors experience. Field data from real devices could be better or worse, and single Lighthouse runs vary from run to run.
This demo's figures are from the US West test region, because that is the region the EnergyX measurement ran in. US East scored higher and is not used.

registry.heading: What the registry found
registry.intro: Putting every published figure in one place, each with what it counts, surfaced cases worth a look. None means a published figure is off. Each is about what a figure says it measures, or about one subject being described in different words on different pages.

cases.heading: Days or hours: one process, several published timings
body: The homepage comparison table gives the DLE processing time as {fact:ex-dle-time}. The FAQ on the same page says hours. Two other EnergyX pages give it as a range of hours to days and as a number of days. All four are shown below, each with where it is published.

Each can be accurate if it measures a different span of the process. None of them says where the clock starts and stops, so a retail investor, or a model summarising the pages, cannot tell them apart.

cases.heading: Funding: two pages, two totals
body: The homepage stats band gives funding as {fact:ex-funding}. The FAQ page answers the question of how much capital EnergyX has raised with a different total, shown below.

Each can be accurate if it counts different things or runs to a different date. Neither says whether its total includes grants or strategic investment, so a retail investor, or a model summarising the pages, cannot tell them apart.

cases.heading: Conventional water use: two pages, two figures
body: The homepage FAQ gives the freshwater used by conventional extraction as {fact:ex-water-conventional}. The sustainability page gives a different figure for brine evaporation, shown below.
Each can be accurate if it describes a different site, year or method. Neither says which it describes, so a reader, or a model summarising the pages, cannot tell them apart.

cases.heading: General Motors: invested in, or engaged with?
body: The homepage FAQ says {fact:ex-gm}. The FAQ page, in its answer about who EnergyX partners with, describes General Motors in different words, shown below.

Both can be accurate, since an investor and a partner can be the same company. Neither page gives an amount, a date or what the relationship consists of, so a retail investor, or a model summarising the pages, cannot tell the two wordings apart.

cases.heading: Water: the claim undersells EnergyX's own figures
body: The homepage FAQ says DLE cuts freshwater use by {fact:ex-water-reduction}. The same FAQ gives the figures behind it: {fact:ex-water-conventional} for conventional extraction, and {fact:ex-water-dle} for EnergyX's process. Those two figures work out to a reduction of {fact:ex-water-implied-reduction}.
The published claim is accurate, just far more modest than the figures beside it. This is the one case where making the figures agree makes EnergyX's claim stronger.

firstWeek.heading: First week on your codebase
firstWeek.intro: If I joined, this is what the first week would look like, in plain terms. None of it changes how the site looks.
points: Measure real visitors' phones alongside the lab numbers, and judge every change by both.
Add a video delivery step: phone-sized, re-encoded video, with no change for the people making it.
Gate each release on performance budgets (Lighthouse CI) and accessibility tests (axe).
Start one registry for every public figure, so each number changes in one place.
Generate llms.txt from it, so AI tools quote the same figures and refer forward-looking questions to IR.
